text:
Garry Kasparov is a world-renowned chess grandmaster, former world champion, and influential political figure. He began studying chess at age seven and rose rapidly through the ranks, winning the Soviet Junior Championship at 13 and becoming the youngest world No. 1 player at age 15. He won the World Chess Championship in 1985 at age 22, defeating Anatoly Karpov in a match widely regarded as one of the greatest in chess history. Kasparov held the world title for 14 years, defeating Karpov in multiple matches, and remained the top-rated player in the world until 2005.
In 1993, Kasparov broke with FIDE (World Chess Federation) over disagreements with its leadership and established the Professional Chess Association (PCA), leading to a split in the world championship title. During this period, he played in numerous high-profile matches and tournaments, including against Nigel Short, Viswanathan Anand, and Vladimir Kramnik. He lost the title to Kramnik in 2000, but remained the world's top-rated player and continued to compete in high-level events.
After retiring from competitive chess in 2005, Kasparov remained active in the chess world, coaching Magnus Carlsen and participating in rapid and blitz events. He also contributed to chess education and published a series of books on chess history and theory, including *My Great Predecessors* . He has been a vocal political figure, advocating for democracy in Russia and criticizing authoritarianism, particularly under Vladimir Putin. He was instrumental in founding the opposition movement "Other Russia" and has consistently spoken out against Russian government actions, including the annexation of Crimea and the invasion of Ukraine. In 2013, he fled Russia due to threats and persecution, and continues to live in exile, criticizing Putin’s regime and advocating for democratic reforms.
Kasparov has also authored books on political and philosophical topics, including *Winter Is Coming* , which argues for a global democratic coalition to counter authoritarianism. He is known for his strong views on human rights, freedom of speech, and the role of intelligence in global politics. His influence extends beyond chess into broader intellectual and political spheres, where he is recognized as a leading voice in the fight for democracy and human rights.
